hero.subtitle: A free live training for adoptive and foster parents, kinship caregivers, and educators who want to help an overwhelmed child feel safe enough to learn.
hero.description:
This training explores how trauma can impact a child's experience in school, including anxiety during transitions, emotional overwhelm in the classroom, and behaviors that are often misunderstood by educators.

Families and professionals will learn how connection, emotional safety, and regulation can support children in building confidence and success at school without relying on fear, shame, or punishment.

countdown.ended: This session has ended. Register to get the replay.

forYou.heading: This is for you if...
items: Your child melts down, shuts down, or "acts out" at school and no one can tell you why.
Mornings, drop-offs, or homework have turned into a daily battle.
You've been told it's "just behavior," but your gut says it's something deeper.
You want to help your child without leaning on fear, shame, or punishment.

learn.heading: What you'll walk away with
items: How trauma actually shows up in the classroom, and why it's so often misread as defiance.
Why transitions and "small" moments can trigger such big reactions.
Simple, love-based ways to bring safety and regulation to your child's school day.
How connection, not consequences, builds the confidence that lasts.

guide.name: Bryan Post
guide.bio: Bryan Post is an internationally recognized expert in adoption, attachment, and trauma, and a leading voice in love-based, family-centered care. For decades he has helped families move from fear and conflict toward connection, calm, and lasting healing.

trust.heading: Why families trust this training
trust.audience: Join adoptive and foster families from across California, supported by the Fear to Love methodology and the Love Pathways Wraparound team.
